title: Rot Detectives: Parent Guide
endLine: Tiny living things make some materials rot faster than others.

scenes.tts: Every autumn, trees drop huge piles of leaves. A year later, many of them seem to be gone. Where did they go? Five sealed containers on a shelf will show your child.
scenes.caption: Every autumn, trees drop huge piles of leaves. A year later, many of them seem to be gone. Where did they go? Five sealed containers on a shelf will show your child.
scenes.visual: Friendly schematic: a big pile of orange and brown autumn leaves under a tree on the left. A small calendar flips a year and the pile shrinks to a thin layer over dark soil. Large text: 'Where did the leaves go?' No photos of real children.
scenes.narration: Every autumn, trees drop huge piles of leaves. A year later, many of them seem to be gone. Where did they go? Five sealed containers on a shelf will show your child.

scenes.visual: The tree and thin leaf layer stay at left. Title 'Rot Detectives' appears for 2 seconds; a single leaf drifts down slowly.

scenes.tts: Set aside about twenty-five minutes. Then check the containers twice a week for three to four weeks. Your child practices looking closely, recording changes, and checking their guesses.
scenes.caption: Set aside about twenty-five minutes. Then check the containers twice a week for three to four weeks. Your child practices looking closely, recording changes, and checking their guesses.
scenes.visual: The view moves to a simple shelf beside the tree. Five clear tubs with lids appear in a row, numbered one to five. Three labels appear one by one: 'Look closely', 'Record changes', 'Wait and check'.
scenes.narration: Set aside about twenty-five minutes. Then check the containers twice a week for three to four weeks. Your child practices looking closely, recording changes, and checking their guesses.

scenes.tts: Number five clear plastic tubs with tight lids. Put two or three spoonfuls of damp soil into each of the first four. Use one item per tub. Add half an apple slice, a dry leaf, bread, and a bottle cap, in that order.
scenes.caption: Number five clear plastic tubs with tight lids. Put two or three spoonfuls of damp soil into each of the first four. Use one item per tub. Add half an apple slice, a dry leaf, bread, and a bottle cap, in that order.
scenes.visual: Same shelf. An adult's hand spoons dark damp soil into tubs one to four. Then, one per tub, the items drop in: half an apple slice, a dry brown leaf, a piece of bread, a plastic bottle cap. Each item settles before its label appears.
scenes.narration: Number five clear plastic tubs with tight lids. Put two or three spoonfuls of damp soil into each of the first four. Use one item per tub. Add half an apple slice, a dry leaf, bread, and a bottle cap, in that order.

scenes.tts: The fifth container gets the other half of the apple and no soil. Tape every lid shut, all the way around. Tell your child, 'These lids stay shut. We are detectives, so we look through the sides.'
scenes.caption: The fifth container gets the other half of the apple and no soil. Tape every lid shut, all the way around. Tell your child, 'These lids stay shut. We are detectives, so we look through the sides.'
scenes.visual: The fifth tub receives the other apple half on its own. Wide clear tape wraps around each lid in turn with a soft shine. A speech bubble: 'We look through the sides.' A magnifying-glass icon hovers beside tub three.
scenes.narration: The fifth container gets the other half of the apple and no soil. Tape every lid shut, all the way around. Tell your child, 'These lids stay shut. We are detectives, so we look through the sides.'

scenes.tts: Before the first check, ask, 'Which one do you think will change first?' Write down the guess together. Have your child draw what each container looks like on day one.
scenes.caption: Before the first check, ask, 'Which one do you think will change first?' Write down the guess together. Have your child draw what each container looks like on day one.
scenes.visual: A simple sheet of paper slides in below the shelf with five boxes; pencil sketches of each tub draw themselves. Speech bubble: 'Which will change first?' A small star marks the child's guess beside one box.
scenes.narration: Before the first check, ask, 'Which one do you think will change first?' Write down the guess together. Have your child draw what each container looks like on day one.

scenes.tts: Now a question for you. After two weeks on a shelf, which containers do you predict will look different? And which one will look exactly the same?
scenes.caption: Now a question for you. After two weeks on a shelf, which containers do you predict will look different? And which one will look exactly the same?
scenes.visual: A calendar above the shelf flips slowly toward 'Week 2', then pauses. All five tubs are shown unchanged with soft question marks over them. Large question card at left: 'Which will change? Which will not?'
scenes.narration: Now a question for you. After two weeks on a shelf, which containers do you predict will look different? And which one will look exactly the same?

scenes.visual: Hold the five unchanged tubs and the question card. Subtle motion: a faint shimmer of moisture on the inside of the lids, and the calendar page trembles without turning.

scenes.tts: Bread often grows fuzzy mold within one to two weeks. Both apples usually rot, even the one with no soil. Mold spores are in the air and on the fruit. The leaf may barely change in a month.
scenes.caption: Bread often grows fuzzy mold within one to two weeks. Both apples usually rot, even the one with no soil. Mold spores are in the air and on the fruit. The leaf may barely change in a month.
scenes.visual: The calendar turns to 'Week 2'. Inside tub three, soft fuzzy green-gray mold patches grow on the bread. Both apple halves show spots and color change. The leaf in tub two looks almost the same. Labels: 'Fast', 'Slow'. Tiny dots drift in the air of tub five to show spores, marked 'schematic'.
scenes.narration: Bread often grows fuzzy mold within one to two weeks. Both apples usually rot, even the one with no soil. Mold spores are in the air and on the fruit. The leaf may barely change in a month.

scenes.tts: The bottle cap can look the same at the end. Most decomposers cannot use plastic as food. Decomposers break down dead things. Here, the main ones are tiny living things like bacteria and mold.
scenes.caption: The bottle cap can look the same at the end. Most decomposers cannot use plastic as food. Decomposers break down dead things. Here, the main ones are tiny living things like bacteria and mold.
scenes.visual: At the end of the shelf timeline, the bottle cap in tub four still looks the same. Beside the bread, a magnified schematic circle shows mold threads and dots representing bacteria. Label the circle 'Decomposers'.
scenes.narration: The bottle cap can look the same at the end. Most decomposers cannot use plastic as food. Decomposers break down dead things. Here, the main ones are tiny living things like bacteria and mold.

scenes.tts: Each time you look, ask, 'What is different since last time?' Compare the apple in soil with the apple on its own. At the end, line up the drawings. Use them to check the starting guess and sort fast, slow, and unchanged results.
scenes.caption: Each time you look, ask, 'What is different since last time?' Compare the apple in soil with the apple on its own. At the end, line up the drawings. Use them to check the starting guess and sort fast, slow, and unchanged results.
scenes.visual: On the shelf, highlight the tubs with the two apple pieces. Line up the day-one and later drawings beneath the tubs. The starting guess stays visible beside the drawings. Sort the drawings under 'Fast', 'Slow', and 'No change'.
scenes.narration: Each time you look, ask, 'What is different since last time?' Compare the apple in soil with the apple on its own. At the end, line up the drawings. Use them to check the starting guess and sort fast, slow, and unchanged results.

scenes.tts: You set up and seal every tub. Keep the tubs on a shelf out of direct sun. Stay with your child and look through the sides. Nobody opens, sniffs, or shakes a tub. Mold spores can set off allergies and asthma. Anyone with asthma, a mold allergy, or a weakened immune system should leave the containers alone. Wash hands after each check.
scenes.caption: You set up and seal every tub. Keep the tubs on a shelf out of direct sun. Stay with your child and look through the sides. Nobody opens, sniffs, or shakes a tub. Mold spores can set off allergies and asthma. Anyone with asthma, a mold allergy, or a weakened immune system should leave the containers alone. Wash hands after each check.
scenes.visual: Back to the shelf. Clear safety badges appear beside it (no more than four): a taped lid with a lock ('Never open'), a nose with a crossed-out sniff ('No sniffing'), soapy hands ('Wash hands'), and a calm adult hand on the shelf ('Adult seals').
scenes.narration: You set up and seal every tub. Keep the tubs on a shelf out of direct sun. Stay with your child and look through the sides. Nobody opens, sniffs, or shakes a tub. Mold spores can set off allergies and asthma. Anyone with asthma, a mold allergy, or a weakened immune system should leave the containers alone. Wash hands after each check.

scenes.tts: A bottle cap, foil ball, or other small piece is a choking risk for children under four. Keep small pieces out of reach. Call nine one one if a child is choking. Never taste the leaf or any food used here. At the end, bag the sealed tubs and put them in the outdoor trash.
scenes.caption: A bottle cap, foil ball, or other small piece is a choking risk for children under four. Keep small pieces out of reach. Call nine one one if a child is choking. Never taste the leaf or any food used here. At the end, bag the sealed tubs and put them in the outdoor trash.
scenes.visual: A crossed-out bottle cap near a small face, labelled 'Under 4: choking risk. Call 911'. Then an adult's hands slide the five sealed tubs into a bag and carry it to an outdoor trash can, lids still taped.
scenes.narration: A bottle cap, foil ball, or other small piece is a choking risk for children under four. Keep small pieces out of reach. Call nine one one if a child is choking. Never taste the leaf or any food used here. At the end, bag the sealed tubs and put them in the outdoor trash.

scenes.tts: So where did all those autumn leaves go? Tiny living things ate them, slowly, and returned the bits to the soil. New plants use those bits to grow.
scenes.caption: So where did all those autumn leaves go? Tiny living things ate them, slowly, and returned the bits to the soil. New plants use those bits to grow.
scenes.visual: The opening tree returns. The thin leaf layer sinks into the soil as small arrows show bits moving down; a green seedling rises from the soil beside the trunk while a few new leaves fall.
scenes.narration: So where did all those autumn leaves go? Tiny living things ate them, slowly, and returned the bits to the soil. New plants use those bits to grow.

scenes.visual: End card over the tree, soil and seedling. Large centered text: 'Tiny living things make some materials rot faster than others.'
scenes.line: Tiny living things make some materials rot faster than others.
